In an abstract set, a ternary equivalence relation determines a collection of equivalence classes or "pencils" that form a linear space in the sense of incidence geometry.  In the same way, a binary equivalence relation on a set determines a partition.
Equivalence test | Equivalence tests are a variation of hypothesis tests used to draw statistical inferences from observed data. If the statistical test indicates the observed data is surprising, assuming that true effects as least as extreme as the equivalence bounds, a Neyman-Pearson approach to statistical inferences can be used to reject effect sizes larger than the equivalence bounds with a pre-specified Type 1 error rate.

A course equivalency can be unilateral, meaning it is deemed equivalent by the receiver.
